figures.caption: Fig. 1 Overview of the target-audit framework. Given user-specified summary statistics, dynamical simulators, parameter distributions, and posterior inference models, the framework evaluates whether real physiological observations are supported by the chosen NMM-SBI pipeline. It sequentially assesses coverage in waveform and summary spaces, posterior recoverability across raw, mechanism, and active targets, and consistency between single-target and joint posteriors. The resulting diagnostic reports identify which targets and interpretive tracks are sufficiently supported for physiological interpretation under the specified modelling choices.
Table 1. Prior distributions and parameter ranges used in the Epileptor simulations. Here, U(·) and N(·) denote the uniform and normal distributions, respectively.

Table 2. Prior distributions and parameter ranges used in the CMC simulations. Here, CN(µ, σ; a, b) denotes a truncated normal distribution with mean µ, standard deviation σ, and truncation interval [a, b].

Fig. 2. Dual-space coverage assessment for Epileptor/iEEG and CMC/MMN. (A) CMC/MMN assessment. The upper-left panel shows example real EEG waveforms exhibiting an evoked MMN response (black) together with simulated data generated by the CMC dynamical model (blue; 50 simulated traces shown for illustration). The lower-left panel shows the mean and standard deviation, across 10 random seeds, of the local-support p values and local-predictive p values in the Summary Space and the Waveform Space for different summary representations. (B) Epileptor/iEEG assessment. The upper-right panel shows example real EEG waveforms from seizures (black) together with simulated data generated by the Epileptor dynamical model (blue; 50 simulated traces shown for illustration). The lower-right panel shows the mean and standard deviation, across 10 random seeds, of the local-support p values and local-predictive p values in the Summary Space and the Waveform Space for different summary representations.

Fig. 3. PSG gains for targets across different tracks and summary representations in the Epileptor/iEEG experiment. Results for the original summary, zero-waveform branch, and waveform branch are reported across all random seeds. Between-group differences were assessed using two-sided paired t-tests matched by random seed. Within each target and summary representation, Holm correction was applied to the three pairwise comparisons. Asterisks indicate the corrected significance levels: q < 0.05 (*), q < 0.01 (**), and q < 0.001 (***).

Within each target and summary representation, Holm correction was applied to the three pairwise comparisons. Asterisks indicate the corrected significance levels: q < 0.05 (*), q < 0.01 (**), and q < 0.001 (***).

Fig. 5. Point-estimate recoverability of candidate targets across the three tracks in the Epileptor/iEEG and CMC/MMN experiments. (A) In the Epileptor/iEEG experiment, the evaluated targets included the raw targets I1, I2, and x0; the mechanism targets ts and tF/S; and the automatically identified active coordinates active 1 and active 2. (B) In the CMC/MMN experiment, the evaluated targets included five raw targets, three predefined mechanism targets, and two active coordinates. Within each group, the columns correspond, in order, to the CNN-LSTM representation, waveform PCA, and model-specific handcrafted features. The final summary group represents the Epileptor core dynamical features in panel A and the preregistered ERP features in panel B. For each summary representation, point-estimate recovery against the blind-test ground truth is quantified using the coefficient of determination R2, the absolute Pearson correlation |ρ|, and 1 − relRMSE. Higher values indicate stronger point-estimate recoverability for all three metrics. Colors represent the mean across 10 random seeds. Negative values of R2 or 1 − relRMSE were truncated to 0 for visualization only.

Table 3. Changes in marginal PSG for each target under the within-track joint posterior relative to the Step 2 single-target posterior in the Epileptor/iEEG experiment. Values are reported as the mean ± standard deviation across 10 random seeds.

Table 4. Changes in marginal PSG for each target under the within-track joint posterior relative to the Step 2 single-target posterior in the CMC/MMN experiment. Values are reported as the mean ± standard deviation across 10 random seeds.

Fig. 6. Within-track posterior synchrony and joint coupling in the Epileptor/iEEG experiment under the CNN-LSTM summary. Panels show the (A) raw, (B) mechanism, and (C) active tracks. The diagonal entries label the targets. The lower-triangular scatter plots show posterior means of target pairs across blind-test observations and random seeds, together with the Pearson correlation coefficient ρmean. Filled and open diamonds indicate whether the bootstrap 95% confidence interval excludes or includes zero, respectively. The upper-triangular histograms show the distribution of target-pair correlations obtained by sampling from the within-track joint posterior while holding each observation fixed. The black line indicates the median, the gray band indicates the bootstrap 95% confidence interval of the median, and the dashed lines mark the descriptive threshold |ρjoint| = 0.3. Pr denotes the proportion of observations satisfying |ρjoint| > 0.3.

Table 5. Active–mechanism directional alignment in the Epileptor/iEEG experiment. sAM h denotes the degree of misalignment between a predefined mechanism direction and the two-dimensional active subspace spanned by active 1 and active 2; lower values indicate stronger absolute geometric alignment. pAM h denotes the empirical upper-tail proportion of the observed alignment within the complete structure-matched permutation reference set; lower values indicate that the mechanism direction is more specific than alternative directions with the same structural constraints. The table reports the median and range across 10 random seeds.

Table 6. Active–mechanism directional alignment in the CMC/MMN experiment. sAM h denotes the degree of misalignment between a predefined mechanism direction and the two-dimensional active subspace spanned by active 1 and active 2; lower values indicate stronger absolute geometric alignment. pAM h denotes the empirical upper-tail proportion of the observed alignment within the complete structure-matched permutation reference set. As above, values near 0.5 indicate that the observed alignment is typical of ordinary structure-matched alternatives and therefore represents the most natural null result, whereas lower values indicate that the mechanism direction is more specific than alternative directions with the same structural constraints. The table reports the median and range across 10 random seeds.

Fig. 12. Cross-track consistency between the raw-posterior push-forward distribution and the directly estimated mechanism posterior. Blue indicates the distribution of the mechanism coordinate obtained by sampling from the raw joint posterior and applying the predefined mechanism function, whereas orange indicates the posterior estimated directly in the mechanism track. The upper curves show kernel density estimates, and the lower step curves show the empirical cumulative distribution functions (ECDFs). The gray area between the two ECDFs equals the one-dimensional 1-Wasserstein distance, W1. Each subplot shows one actual observation whose W1 is closest to the cross-seed central value for the corresponding summary–mechanism combination. The values in the lower-right corner of each subplot report the median ± standard deviation across 10 random seeds. pRM i denotes the empirical upper-tail proportion obtained from an independent simulation-based calibration set. Values near 0.5 indicate that the observed discrepancy is typical of ordinary simulated observations, whereas low values indicate that the disagreement between the two inference paths exceeds the range of normal inference error. (A) CMC/MMN experiment. (B) Epileptor/SOZ-local iEEG experiment.
